name: Bruus North Friesland
description: Bruus North Friesland is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from North Friesland in northern Germany. It uses a 36-card French-suited pack with wildly disturbed card rankings, daring and striking bonuses, and a race to a target score tracked with matchsticks.

content.text: Bruus North Friesland is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from North Friesland in northern Germany. It uses a 36-card French-suited pack with wildly disturbed card rankings, daring and striking bonuses, and a race to a target score tracked with matchsticks.

Bruus is a north German card game originating in North Friesland and neighbouring Schleswig. It descends from the medieval Karnöffel family and has been played for over 300 years, reaching particular popularity around Hamburg before surviving in a few villages near Husum and Treia.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Optional

Type: Standard 52-card deck

items.text: Treia Variant: Treia choir players use a 32-card Skat pack with eight tricks and play a shorter game to ten matches, with local rituals around scoring and schnapps penalties.
Two- and Six-Player Bruus: House rules allow two-hand Bruus and six-player Bruus in teams of three, adjusting only the number of players and tricks while keeping the core Bruus mechanics.
